Google Introduces Agent Executor (AX): A New Framework for Agentic Orchestration

Overview of Agent Executor (AX)

Google has introduced Agent Executor (AX), an open-source orchestration runtime designed specifically for managing autonomous agent workloads. Built to function at a massive scale, AX addresses the unique challenges of agentic computing, such as state management, sandbox isolation, and the prevention of runaway API costs.

Why AX Was Built

Unlike traditional stateless microservices or simple batch jobs, autonomous agents accumulate state and require persistent monitoring. According to project documentation, AX provides a declarative approach to managing these workloads, drawing design inspiration from Kubernetes to provide a familiar experience for developers and infrastructure engineers.

Key Features

AX offers a set of primitives designed to handle the complexities of agent orchestration:

  • Declarative Manifests: Tasks are defined using `ax.io/v1alpha1` manifests, allowing for version-controlled, repeatable deployments.
  • Sandboxed Execution: AX relies on Agent Substrate to ensure that agent tasks run in isolated, secure environments within a cluster.
  • Kubernetes-Style CLI: The AX command-line interface is designed to mimic `kubectl`, supporting commands like `apply`, `get`, `describe`, and `delete`, along with specialized verbs for agent interaction.
  • Scalability: The architecture is built to support millions of autonomous tasks per cluster.

Practical Implications and Setup

AX is currently under heavy development. Users should expect significant breaking changes as protocols and specifications are refined before a stable release.

To implement AX, a Kubernetes cluster with Agent Substrate installed is required. Deployment involves:

  • Authenticating with a container registry (using Podman or Docker).
  • Configuring the AX control plane to interface with the Substrate Control API.
  • Deploying the server components via the `ax-system` namespace.

For those looking to evaluate the framework, a demonstration script is provided in the repository to guide users through the lifecycle of a custom workspace, including readiness checks and task suspension.

How to Verify

Interested parties can review the source code, installation guides, and documentation on the official AX GitHub repository. As the project is in early-stage development, users are encouraged to monitor the repository for updates, API changes, and community-reported issues.
